sanskrit: tatra taṃ sarvabhūtāni vismitāny abruvaṃs tadā surūpaṃ patram ālakṣya suparṇo 'yaṃ bhavatv iti
english: There all living beings, astonished, spoke at that time upon beholding that beautiful bird: 'Let this be Suparṇa.'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tad adbhutaṃ cāpi sahasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ khago mahad idaṃ bhūtam iti matvābhyabhāṣata
english: And seeing that marvel, Sahasrākṣa, the destroyer of cities, reflecting that this bird is a great being, addressed him.

sanskrit: balaṃ vijñātum icchāmi yat te param anuttamam sakhyaṃ cānantam icchāmi tvayā saha khagottama
english: 'I wish to know the strength that is supreme and unsurpassed in you, and I desire an eternal friendship with you, O best of birds.'

sanskrit: garuḍa uvāca sakhyaṃ me 'stu tvayā deva yathecchasi puraṃdara balaṃ tu mama jānīhi mahac cāsahyam eva ca
english: Garuḍa said: 'Let there be friendship between you and me, O god, as you wish, O Purandara. But know my strength to be great and truly unbearable.'

sanskrit: kāmaṃ naitat praśaṃsanti santaḥ svabalasaṃstavam guṇasaṃkīrtanaṃ cāpi svayam eva śatakrato
english: 'Indeed, the virtuous do not commend self-praise of one's own strength, nor the recounting of one's own virtues by oneself, O Śatakratu.'

sanskrit: sakheti kṛtvā tu sakhe pṛṣṭo vakṣyāmy ahaṃ tvayā na hy ātmastavasaṃyuktaṃ vaktavyam animittataḥ
english: 'But since you, O friend, treating me as a friend have asked me, I shall tell you; for that which is mixed with self-praise ought not to be spoken without reason.'

sanskrit: saparvatavanām urvīṃ sasāgaravanām imām pakṣanāḍyaikayā śakra tvāṃ caivātrāvalambinam
english: 'This broad earth with its mountains and forests, and this ocean with its forests, and you yourself clinging here — all this with a single sinew of my wing, O Śakra —'

sanskrit: sarvān saṃpiṇḍitān vāpi lokān sasthāṇujaṅgamān vaheyam apariśrānto viddhīdaṃ me mahad balam
english: '— or all the worlds gathered together with their stationary and moving beings, I could carry without fatigue. Know this to be my great strength.'

sanskrit: sūta uvāca ity uktavacanaṃ vīraṃ kirīṭī śrīmatāṃ varaḥ āha śaunaka devendraḥ sarvabhūtahitaḥ prabhuḥ
english: The Sūta said: To that hero who had spoken thus, O Śaunaka, the diadem-wearer, best of the glorious, the lord Indra, benefactor of all beings, replied.

sanskrit: pratigṛhyatām idānīṃ me sakhyam ānantyam uttamam na kāryaṃ tava somena mama somaḥ pradīyatām asmāṃs te hi prabādheyur yebhyo dadyād bhavān imam
english: 'Let this supreme and eternal friendship of mine be accepted now. You have no need of the Soma; give the Soma to me — for those from whom you would give it would trouble us.'

sanskrit: garuḍa uvāca kiṃ cit kāraṇam uddiśya somo 'yaṃ nīyate mayā na dāsyāmi samādātuṃ somaṃ kasmai cid apy aham
english: Garuḍa said: 'For a certain reason I am carrying this Soma. I will not give it to anyone whatsoever to take away.'

sanskrit: yatremaṃ tu sahasrākṣa nikṣipeyam ahaṃ svayam tvam ādāya tatas tūrṇaṃ harethās tridaśeśvara
english: 'But wherever I myself set it down, O Sahasrākṣa, then you swiftly take it away, O lord of the thirty gods.'

sanskrit: śakra uvāca vākyenānena tuṣṭo 'haṃ yat tvayoktam ihāṇḍaja yad icchasi varaṃ mattas tad gṛhāṇa khagottama
english: Śakra said: 'I am pleased by this speech you have spoken here, O born-of-an-egg. Whatever boon you desire from me, take it, O best of birds.'

sanskrit: sūta uvāca ity uktaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ kadrūputrān anusmaran smṛtvā caivopadhikṛtaṃ mātur dāsyanimittataḥ
english: The Sūta said: Thus addressed, he replied thus, remembering the sons of Kadrū, and also recalling the deception done regarding his mother's enslavement.

sanskrit: īśo 'ham api sarvasya kariṣyāmi tu te 'rthitām bhaveyur bhujagāḥ śakra mama bhakṣyā mahābalāḥ
english: 'I am master of all, and I shall fulfil your request as well. O Śakra, may the mighty serpents become my food.'

sanskrit: tathety uktvānvagacchat taṃ tato dānavasūdanaḥ hariṣyāmi vinikṣiptaṃ somam ity anubhāṣya tam
english: Having said 'So be it,' the slayer of demons then followed him, saying to him: 'I shall take the Soma once it is set down.'

sanskrit: ājagāma tatas tūrṇaṃ suparṇo mātur antikam atha sarpān uvācedaṃ sarvān paramahṛṣṭavat
english: Then Suparṇa came swiftly to his mother's side, and then addressed all the serpents thus, with great joy.

sanskrit: idam ānītam amṛtaṃ nikṣepsyāmi kuśeṣu vaḥ snātā maṅgalasaṃyuktās tataḥ prāśnīta pannagāḥ
english: 'This amṛta I have brought I shall place on the kuśa grass for you. Having bathed and performed auspicious rites, then eat it, O serpents.'

sanskrit: adāsī caiva māteyam adyaprabhṛti cāstu me yathoktaṃ bhavatām etad vaco me pratipāditam
english: 'And this mother shall be a slave no longer; from this day let her be free to me. The word I gave to you has been fulfilled.'

sanskrit: tataḥ snātuṃ gatāḥ sarpāḥ pratyuktvā taṃ tathety uta śakro 'py amṛtam ākṣipya jagāma tridivaṃ punaḥ
english: Then the serpents went to bathe, having replied to him 'So be it.' And Śakra, snatching up the amṛta, returned again to the triple heaven.

sanskrit: athāgatās tam uddeśaṃ sarpāḥ somārthinas tadā snātāś ca kṛtajapyāś ca prahṛṣṭāḥ kṛtamaṅgalāḥ
english: Then the serpents, desiring the Soma, came to that spot — having bathed, performed their recitations, joyful, and having performed auspicious rites.

sanskrit: tad vijñāya hṛtaṃ sarpāḥ pratimāyākṛtaṃ ca tat somasthānam idaṃ ceti darbhāṃs te lilihus tadā
english: The serpents, knowing that it had been taken away and that it was a mere semblance, and that this was the place where the Soma had been, then licked the kuśa grass.

sanskrit: tato dvaidhīkṛtā jihvā sarpāṇāṃ tena karmaṇā abhavaṃś cāmṛtasparśād darbhās te 'tha pavitriṇaḥ
english: Thereupon, by that act, the tongues of the serpents became forked. And those blades of kuśa grass, from the touch of the amṛta, became sacred.

sanskrit: tataḥ suparṇaḥ paramaprahṛṣṭavān; vihṛtya mātrā saha tatra kānane bhujaṃgabhakṣaḥ paramārcitaḥ khagair; ahīnakīrtir vinatām anandayat
english: Then Suparṇa, supremely joyful, having sported with his mother in that forest — the devourer of serpents, greatly honoured by the birds, his glory unblemished — made Vinatā rejoice.

sanskrit: imāṃ kathāṃ yaḥ śṛṇuyān naraḥ sadā; paṭheta vā dvijajanamukhyasaṃsadi asaṃśayaṃ tridivam iyāt sa puṇyabhāṅ; mahātmanaḥ patagapateḥ prakīrtanāt
english: Whoever constantly hears this tale or recites it in an assembly of leading brāhmaṇas shall, without doubt, attain the triple heaven, gaining merit through the glorification of the great-souled lord of birds.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca bhujaṃgamānāṃ śāpasya mātrā caiva sutena ca vinatāyās tvayā proktaṃ kāraṇaṃ sūtanandana
english: Śaunaka said: 'The cause of the curse on the serpents, and of the mother and her son, and of Vinatā, O son of a Sūta, you have narrated.'

sanskrit: varapradānaṃ bhartrā ca kadrūvinatayos tathā nāmanī caiva te prokte pakṣiṇor vainateyayoḥ
english: 'The granting of boons by the husband to Kadrū and Vinatā, and also the names of the two birds born of Vinatā, have been told by you.'

sanskrit: pannagānāṃ tu nāmāni na kīrtayasi sūtaja prādhānyenāpi nāmāni śrotum icchāmahe vayam
english: 'But the names of the serpents you do not recite, O son of a Sūta. We wish to hear the principal names as well.'

sanskrit: sūta uvāca bahutvān nāmadheyāni bhujagānāṃ tapodhana na kīrtayiṣye sarveṣāṃ prādhānyena tu me śṛṇu
english: The Sūta said: 'Because of the great number of names of the serpents, O wealth of asceticism, I shall not recite all of them. Hear from me only the principal ones.'

sanskrit: śeṣaḥ prathamato jāto vāsukis tadanantaram airāvatas takṣakaś ca karkoṭakadhanaṃjayau
english: Śeṣa was born first, then Vāsuki; and Airāvata, Takṣaka, and Karkoṭaka and Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: kāliyo maṇināgaś ca nāgaś cāpūraṇas tathā nāgas tathā piñjaraka elāpatro 'tha vāmanaḥ
english: Kālīya and Maṇināga, and the serpent Apūraṇa, and also the serpent Piñjaraka, then Elāpatra and Vāmana.

sanskrit: nīlānīlau tathā nāgau kalmāṣaśabalau tathā āryakaś cādikaś caiva nāgaś ca śalapotakaḥ
english: The two serpents Nīla and Anīla, and also Kalmāṣa and Śabala, and Āryaka and Ādika, and also the serpent Śalapotaka.

sanskrit: sumanomukho dadhimukhas tathā vimalapiṇḍakaḥ āptaḥ koṭanakaś caiva śaṅkho vālaśikhas tathā
english: Sumanomukha and Dadhimukha, and also Vimalapiṇḍaka; Āpta and also Koṭanaka, Śaṅkha and Vālaśikha as well.

sanskrit: niṣṭhyūnako hemaguho nahuṣaḥ piṅgalas tathā bāhyakarṇo hastipadas tathā mudgarapiṇḍakaḥ
english: Niṣṭhyūnaka, Hemaguha, Nahuṣa and Piṅgala, Bāhyakarṇa and Hastipada, and also Mudgarapiṇḍaka.

sanskrit: kambalāśvatarau cāpi nāgaḥ kālīyakas tathā vṛttasaṃvartakau nāgau dvau ca padmāv iti śrutau
english: Kambala and Aśvatara, and also the serpent Kālīyaka, and the two serpents Vṛtta and Saṃvartaka, and two known as the Padmas.

sanskrit: nāgaḥ śaṅkhanakaś caiva tathā ca sphaṇḍako 'paraḥ kṣemakaś ca mahānāgo nāgaḥ piṇḍārakas tathā
english: The serpent Śaṅkhanaka, and also another named Sphaṇḍaka; the great serpent Kṣemaka and the serpent Piṇḍāraka as well.

sanskrit: karavīraḥ puṣpadaṃṣṭra eḷako bilvapāṇḍukaḥ mūṣakādaḥ śaṅkhaśirāḥ pūrṇadaṃṣṭro haridrakaḥ
english: Karavīra, Puṣpadaṃṣṭra, Eḷaka, Bilvapāṇḍuka, Mūṣakāda, Śaṅkhaśiras, Pūrṇadaṃṣṭra, and Haridraka.

sanskrit: aparājito jyotikaś ca pannagaḥ śrīvahas tathā kauravyo dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca puṣkaraḥ śalyakas tathā
english: Aparājita, Jyotika the serpent, and Śrīvaha; Kauravya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Puṣkara, and also Śalyaka.

sanskrit: virajāś ca subāhuś ca śālipiṇḍaś ca vīryavān hastibhadraḥ piṭharako mukharaḥ koṇavāsanaḥ
english: Virajā, Subāhu, and the mighty Śālipiṇḍa, Hastibhadra, Pīṭharaka, Mukhara, and Koṇavāsana.

sanskrit: kuñjaraḥ kuraraś caiva tathā nāgaḥ prabhākaraḥ kumudaḥ kumudākṣaś ca tittirir halikas tathā karkarākarkarau cobhau kuṇḍodaramahodarau
english: Kuñjara, Kurara, and also the serpent Prabhākara, Kumuda and Kumudākṣa, Tittiri and Halika, and both Karkara and Akarkara, and Kuṇḍodara and Mahodara.

sanskrit: ete prādhānyato nāgāḥ kīrtitā dvijasattama bahutvān nāmadheyānām itare na prakīrtitāḥ
english: These serpents have been named in order of prominence, O best of twice-born. Because of the great number of names, the others have not been recited.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ prasavo yaś ca prasavasya ca saṃtatiḥ asaṃkhyeyeti matvā tān na bravīmi dvijottama
english: The offspring of these, and the lineages of those offspring — regarding them I do not speak, O best of twice-born, deeming them to be without number.

sanskrit: bahūnīha sahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca aśakyāny eva saṃkhyātuṃ bhujagānāṃ tapodhana
english: Many thousands, millions, and tens of millions here — truly impossible to count — are the serpents, O wealth of asceticism.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca jātā vai bhujagās tāta vīryavanto durāsadāḥ śāpaṃ taṃ tv atha vijñāya kṛtavanto nu kiṃ param
english: Śaunaka said: 'Indeed the serpents were born, O dear one, mighty and unapproachable. But having come to know that curse, what did they do next?'

sanskrit: sūta uvāca teṣāṃ tu bhagavāñ śeṣas tyaktvā kadrūṃ mahāyaśāḥ tapo vipulam ātasthe vāyubhakṣo yatavrataḥ
english: The Sūta said: Among them, the blessed Śeṣa of great renown, abandoning Kadrū, undertook vast austerities, living on air, with restrained vows.

sanskrit: gandhamādanam āsādya badaryāṃ ca taporataḥ gokarṇe puṣkarāraṇye tathā himavatas taṭe
english: Reaching Gandhamādana, and Badarī, intent on asceticism; at Gokarṇa, in the forest of Puṣkara, and on the slopes of the Himālayas.

sanskrit: teṣu teṣu ca puṇyeṣu tīrtheṣv āyataneṣu ca ekāntaśīlī niyataḥ satataṃ vijitendriyaḥ
english: In those various holy tīrthas and sacred shrines, living in solitude, disciplined, constantly, with his senses conquered.

sanskrit: tapyamānaṃ tapo ghoraṃ taṃ dadarśa pitāmahaḥ pariśuṣkamāṃsatvaksnāyuṃ jaṭācīradharaṃ prabhum
english: The Grandfather beheld him practising terrible austerities — the lord, his flesh, skin, and sinews withered, wearing matted locks and bark garments.

sanskrit: tam abravīt satyadhṛtiṃ tapyamānaṃ pitāmahaḥ kim idaṃ kuruṣe śeṣa prajānāṃ svasti vai kuru
english: The Grandfather spoke to him, holding to truth, as he performed austerities: 'What is this you are doing, Śeṣa? Ensure the well-being of living creatures.'

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi tīvreṇa tapasā prajās tāpayase 'nagha brūhi kāmaṃ ca me śeṣa yat te hṛdi ciraṃ sthitam
english: 'For with your fierce austerity you cause affliction to living creatures, O sinless one. Tell me your desire, O Śeṣa — that which has long been lodged in your heart.'

sanskrit: śeṣa uvāca sodaryā mama sarve hi bhrātaro mandacetasaḥ saha tair notsahe vastuṃ tad bhavān anumanyatām
english: Śeṣa said: 'All my brothers from the same mother are of dull mind. I have no desire to live with them — may Your Honour consent to this.'

sanskrit: abhyasūyanti satataṃ parasparam amitravat tato 'haṃ tapa ātiṣṭhe naitān paśyeyam ity uta
english: 'They constantly envy one another like enemies; therefore I practise austerity, thinking: may I not see them.'

sanskrit: na marṣayanti satataṃ vinatāṃ sasutāṃ ca te asmākaṃ cāparo bhrātā vainateyaḥ pitāmaha
english: 'They constantly do not endure Vinatā and her son, and our other brother Vainateya, O Grandfather.'

sanskrit: taṃ ca dviṣanti te 'tyarthaṃ sa cāpi sumahābalaḥ varapradānāt sa pituḥ kaśyapasya mahātmanaḥ
english: 'They hate him exceedingly, and he too is of very great strength, by virtue of the boon from his father, the great-souled Kaśyapa.'

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tapaḥ samāsthāya mokṣyāmīdaṃ kalevaram kathaṃ me pretyabhāve 'pi na taiḥ syāt saha saṃgamaḥ
english: 'Therefore I, having undertaken austerity, shall abandon this body — so that even after death there may be no association with them for me.'

sanskrit: brahmovāca jānāmi śeṣa sarveṣāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ te viceṣṭitam mātuś cāpy aparādhād vai bhrātṝṇāṃ te mahad bhayam
english: Brahmā said: 'I know, O Śeṣa, the conduct of all your brothers. And from the fault of your mother there is indeed great danger for your brothers.'

sanskrit: kṛto 'tra parihāraś ca pūrvam eva bhujaṃgama bhrātṝṇāṃ tava sarveṣāṃ na śokaṃ kartum arhasi
english: 'And a remedy has already been arranged here beforehand, O serpent. For all of your brothers, you ought not to grieve.'

sanskrit: vṛṇīṣva ca varaṃ mattaḥ śeṣa yat te 'bhikāṅkṣitam ditsāmi hi varaṃ te 'dya prītir me paramā tvayi
english: 'And choose a boon from me, O Śeṣa, whatever you desire. For I will grant you a boon today; my pleasure in you is supreme.'

sanskrit: diṣṭyā ca buddhir dharme te niviṣṭā pannagottama ato bhūyaś ca te buddhir dharme bhavatu susthirā
english: 'By good fortune your mind is fixed on dharma, O best of serpents. Therefore may your mind be firmly stable in dharma even more.'

sanskrit: śeṣa uvāca eṣa eva varo me 'dya kāṅkṣitaḥ prapitāmaha dharme me ramatāṃ buddhiḥ śame tapasi ceśvara
english: Śeṣa said: 'This very thing is the boon I desire today, O Great-grandfather: may my mind delight in dharma, in tranquillity, and in austerity, O Lord.'

sanskrit: brahmovāca prīto 'smy anena te śeṣa damena praśamena ca tvayā tv idaṃ vacaḥ kāryaṃ manniyogāt prajāhitam
english: Brahmā said: 'I am pleased by this self-restraint and tranquillity of yours, O Śeṣa. But this task must be done by you, by my command, for the welfare of living beings.'

sanskrit: imāṃ mahīṃ śailavanopapannāṃ; sasāgarāṃ sākarapattanāṃ ca tvaṃ śeṣa samyak calitāṃ yathāvat; saṃgṛhya tiṣṭhasva yathācalā syāt
english: 'This earth adorned with mountains and forests, with its oceans, with its towns and cities — O Śeṣa, support it properly as it trembles, so that it may be steady.'

sanskrit: śeṣa uvāca yathāha devo varadaḥ prajāpatir; mahīpatir bhūtapatir jagatpatiḥ tathā mahīṃ dhārayitāsmi niścalāṃ; prayaccha tāṃ me śirasi prajāpate
english: Śeṣa said: 'As the god, the granter of boons, the lord of beings, the lord of the earth, the lord of the world commands, so shall I hold the earth steady. Place it upon my head, O Lord of beings.'

sanskrit: brahmovāca adho mahīṃ gaccha bhujaṃgamottama; svayaṃ tavaiṣā vivaraṃ pradāsyati imāṃ dharāṃ dhārayatā tvayā hi me; mahat priyaṃ śeṣa kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Brahmā said: 'Go beneath the earth, O best of serpents — she herself will give you an opening. By you holding this earth up, a great favour will be done for me, O Śeṣa.'

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tatheti kṛtvā vivaraṃ praviśya sa; prabhur bhuvo bhujagavarāgrajaḥ sthitaḥ bibharti devīṃ śirasā mahīm imāṃ; samudranemiṃ parigṛhya sarvataḥ
english: The Sūta said: Having said 'So be it,' he entered the opening. That lord of the earth, the foremost of the best of serpents, stands there, bearing on his head this goddess Earth, grasping her with her ocean-rim on all sides.

sanskrit: brahmovāca śeṣo 'si nāgottama dharmadevo; mahīm imāṃ dhārayase yad ekaḥ anantabhogaḥ parigṛhya sarvāṃ; yathāham evaṃ balabhid yathā vā
english: Brahmā said: 'You are Śeṣa, O best of serpents, the god of dharma. You alone bear this earth with your infinite coils encompassing it all — even as I do, even as Balabhit does.'

sanskrit: sūta uvāca adho bhūmer vasaty evaṃ nāgo 'nantaḥ pratāpavān dhārayan vasudhām ekaḥ śāsanād brahmaṇo vibhuḥ
english: The Sūta said: Thus the serpent Ananta, powerful in might, dwells beneath the earth, holding the earth alone, the mighty one, by Brahmā's command.

sanskrit: suparṇaṃ ca sakhāyaṃ vai bhagavān amarottamaḥ prādād anantāya tadā vainateyaṃ pitāmahaḥ
english: And the blessed Grandfather, best of the immortals, then granted Suparṇa, the son of Vinatā, as a friend to Ananta.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca mātuḥ sakāśāt taṃ śāpaṃ śrutvā pannagasattamaḥ vāsukiś cintayām āsa śāpo 'yaṃ na bhavet katham
english: The Sūta said: Having heard that curse from their mother, the best of serpents, Vāsuki, began to think: 'How may this curse not come to pass?'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa mantrayām āsa bhrātṛbhiḥ saha sarvaśaḥ airāvataprabhṛtibhir ye sma dharmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Then he took counsel on all sides with his brothers led by Airāvata — those who were devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: vāsukir uvāca ayaṃ śāpo yathoddiṣṭo viditaṃ vas tathānaghāḥ tasya śāpasya mokṣārthaṃ mantrayitvā yatāmahe
english: Vāsuki said: 'This curse as declared you all know, O sinless ones. For the sake of release from that curse, having deliberated, let us strive.'

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva śāpānāṃ pratighāto hi vidyate na tu mātrābhiśaptānāṃ mokṣo vidyeta pannagāḥ
english: 'For all curses there is a counter-remedy; yet there may be no release for those who have been cursed by their own mother, O serpents.'

sanskrit: avyayasyāprameyasya satyasya ca tathāgrataḥ śaptā ity eva me śrutvā jāyate hṛdi vepathuḥ
english: 'Upon hearing that we were cursed in the presence of the Imperishable, the Immeasurable, and Truth itself, a trembling arises in my heart.'

sanskrit: nūnaṃ sarvavināśo 'yam asmākaṃ samudāhṛtaḥ na hy enāṃ so 'vyayo devaḥ śapantīṃ pratyaṣedhayat
english: 'Surely this our complete destruction has been proclaimed. For that imperishable god did not restrain her as she cursed.'

sanskrit: tasmāt saṃmantrayāmo 'tra bhujagānām anāmayam yathā bhaveta sarveṣāṃ mā naḥ kālo 'tyagād ayam
english: 'Therefore let us deliberate here on the welfare of the serpents, so that it may be for all of us; let not this time pass us by.'

sanskrit: api mantrayamāṇā hi hetuṃ paśyāma mokṣaṇe yathā naṣṭaṃ purā devā gūḍham agniṃ guhāgatam
english: 'Even while deliberating we may perceive a means for deliverance — just as the gods once found the hidden fire that had entered a cave.'

sanskrit: yathā sa yajño na bhaved yathā vāpi parābhavet janamejayasya sarpāṇāṃ vināśakaraṇāya hi
english: 'Such that that sacrifice may not take place, or such that it may be defeated — the sacrifice of Janamejaya that is the instrument of the serpents' destruction.'

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tathety uktvā tu te sarve kādraveyāḥ samāgatāḥ samayaṃ cakrire tatra mantrabuddhiviśāradāḥ
english: The Sūta said: Saying 'So be it,' all those sons of Kadrū assembled together and made a compact there — skilled in the wisdom of counsel.

sanskrit: eke tatrābruvan nāgā vayaṃ bhūtvā dvijarṣabhāḥ janamejayaṃ taṃ bhikṣāmo yajñas te na bhaved iti
english: Some of the serpents there said: 'Let us become foremost brāhmaṇas and beg Janamejaya, saying: may your sacrifice not take place.'

sanskrit: apare tv abruvan nāgās tatra paṇḍitamāninaḥ mantriṇo 'sya vayaṃ sarve bhaviṣyāmaḥ susaṃmatāḥ
english: But other serpents there, fancying themselves learned, said: 'All of us shall become his trusted ministers, well esteemed.'
